36.en: The unprecedented land clearance released vast quantities of carbon dioxide into the atmosphere, triggering for the first time humanly caused global warming.
parts: 这场规模空前的土地清垦向大气释放了大量二氧化碳，首次引发了由人类活动造成的全球变暖。

37.en: Temperatures climbed more rapidly in the twentieth century as the use of fossil fuels proliferated and greenhouse gas levels continued to soar.
parts: 到了20世纪，随着化石燃料的使用日益普遍、大气中温室气体的含量不断猛增，气温上升得更快了。

38.en: The rise has been even steeper since the early 1980s.
parts: 自20世纪80年代初以来，升温的势头更猛了。

39.en: The Little Ice Age has given way to a new climatic regime, marked by prolonged and steady warming.
parts: 小冰期已经过去，接替它的是一种新的气候状态，其特征是长期而持续的变暖。

40.en: At the same time, extreme weather events like Category 5 hurricanes are becoming more frequent.
parts: 与此同时，五级飓风等极端天气事件也越来越频繁。

48.en: A laser thunder factory could shake the moisture out of clouds, perhaps preventing the formation of the giant hailstones that threaten crops.
parts: 用激光制造雷电的装置有可能震落云中的水分，或许还能阻止威胁农作物的巨大冰雹形成。

1.en: Seldom is the weather more dramatic than when thunderstorms strike.
parts: 很少有哪种天气像雷暴来袭时那样惊心动魄。

2.en: Their electrical fury inflicts death or serious injury on around 500 people each year in the United States alone.
parts: 单在美国，雷暴猛烈的放电每年就会造成约500人死亡或重伤。

3.en: As the clouds roll in, a leisurely round of golf can become a terrifying dice with death - out in the open, a lone golfer may be a lightning bolt’s most inviting target.
parts: 乌云涌来，原本悠闲的一轮高尔夫球也可能变成一场惊险的生死赌局。
在开阔地带，独自打球的人可能最容易成为闪电的目标。

4.en: And there is damage to property too.
parts: 雷电还会造成财产损失。

5.en: Lightning damage costs American power companies more than $100 million a year.
parts: 雷电造成的损害每年给美国电力公司带来超过一亿美元的损失。

6.en: But researchers in the United States and Japan are planning to hit back.
parts: 不过，美国和日本的研究人员正计划反击。

7.en: Already in laboratory trials they have tested strategies for neutralising the power of thunderstorms, and this winter they will brave real storms, equipped with an armoury of lasers that they will be pointing towards the heavens to discharge thunderclouds before lightning can strike.
parts: 他们已经在实验室里测试过削弱雷暴威力的办法。
今年冬天，他们将带着一整套激光设备直面真正的风暴，
把激光射向天空，争取在雷击发生前让雷云释放电荷。

8.en: The idea of forcing storm clouds to discharge their lightning on command is not new.
parts: 让雷云按人的指令放电，这个想法并不新鲜。

9.en: In the early 1960s, researchers tried firing rockets trailing wires into thunderclouds to set up an easy discharge path for the huge electric charges that these clouds generate.
parts: 20世纪60年代初，研究人员试着把拖着导线的火箭射入雷云，
想为云中产生的大量电荷提供一条易于放电的通路。

10.en: The technique survives to this day at a test site in Florida run by the University of Florida, with support from the Electrical Power Research Institute (EPRI), based in California.
parts: 佛罗里达大学运营的一个试验场至今仍在使用这项技术，
位于加利福尼亚州的电力研究所（EPRI）为其提供支持。

11.en: EPRI, which is funded by power companies, is looking at ways to protect the United States’ power grid from lightning strikes.
parts: 电力研究所由电力公司资助，正在研究怎样保护美国电网免遭雷击。

12.en: ‘We can cause the lightning to strike where we want it to using rockets,’ says Ralph Bernstein, manager of lightning projects at EPRI.
parts: 电力研究所雷电项目负责人拉尔夫·伯恩斯坦说：“利用火箭，我们能让闪电击中指定的地方。”

13.en: The rocket site is providing precise measurements of lightning voltages and allowing engineers to check how electrical equipment bears up.
parts: 在这个火箭试验场，可以精确测量雷电电压，也能让工程师检验电气设备能否经受住雷击。

14.en: Bad behaviour.
parts: 不听使唤的闪电
terms: 不听使唤的表现（小标题）

15.en: But while rockets are fine for research, they cannot provide the protection from lightning strikes that everyone is looking for.
parts: 不过，火箭虽然用于研究很合适，却无法提供人们想要的防雷保护。

16.en: The rockets cost around $1,200 each, can only be fired at a limited frequency and their failure rate is about 40 per cent.
parts: 每枚火箭约需1200美元，发射频率有限，而且失败率约为40%。

17.en: And even when they do trigger lightning, things still do not always go according to plan.
parts: 即便火箭确实引发了闪电，事情仍未必能按计划发展。

18.en: ‘Lightning is not perfectly well behaved,’ says Bernstein.
parts: “闪电并不总是那么听话，”伯恩斯坦说。

19.en: ‘Occasionally, it will take a branch and go someplace it wasn’t supposed to go.’
parts: “偶尔它会分出一支，击中本来不该击中的地方。”

20.en: And anyway, who would want to fire streams of rockets in a populated area?
parts: 况且，谁愿意在人口聚居的地方接连发射火箭呢？

21.en: ‘What goes up must come down,’ points out Jean-Claude Diels of the University of New Mexico.
parts: “射上去的东西总要掉下来，”新墨西哥大学的让-克洛德·迪尔斯指出。

22.en: Diels is leading a project, which is backed by EPRI, to try to use lasers to discharge lightning safely - and safety is a basic requirement since no one wants to put themselves or their expensive equipment at risk.
parts: 迪尔斯正主持电力研究所支持的一个项目，尝试用激光让雷云安全放电。
安全是基本要求，因为谁也不想让自己或昂贵的设备面临危险。

23.en: With around $500,000 invested so far, a promising system is just emerging from the laboratory.
parts: 到目前为止，已投入约50万美元，一套颇有前景的系统刚刚开始走出实验室。

24.en: The idea began some 20 years ago, when high-powered lasers were revealing their ability to extract electrons out of atoms and create ions.
parts: 这个想法始于约20年前，当时高功率激光正显现出从原子中剥离电子、形成离子的能力。

25.en: If a laser could generate a line of ionisation in the air all the way up to a storm cloud, this conducting path could be used to guide lightning to Earth, before the electric field becomes strong enough to break down the air in an uncontrollable surge.
parts: 如果激光能在空气中形成一条直达雷云的电离通道，
就可以利用这条导电通道把闪电引向地面，
赶在电场强到使空气击穿、引发失控的电流冲击之前。

26.en: To stop the laser itself being struck, it would not be pointed straight at the clouds.
parts: 为了防止激光器本身遭到雷击，激光不会直接对准云层。

27.en: Instead it would be directed at a mirror, and from there into the sky.
parts: 激光会先射向一面镜子，再从那里反射到空中。

28.en: The mirror would be protected by placing lightning conductors close by.
parts: 在镜子附近安装避雷装置，就能保护镜子。

29.en: Ideally, the cloud-zapper (gun) would be cheap enough to be installed around all key power installations, and portable enough to be taken to international sporting events to beam up at brewing storm clouds.
parts: 理想情况下，这种雷云放电装置的造价会足够低，以便在所有重要电力设施周围安装；
同时它也要足够便携，能带到国际体育赛事现场，向正在形成的雷雨云发射激光。

30.en: A stumbling block.
parts: 一道难关

31.en: However, there is still a big stumbling block.
parts: 不过，目前还有一大障碍。

32.en: The laser is no nifty portable: it’s a monster that takes up a whole room.
parts: 这台激光器可不是什么小巧的便携设备。它是个庞然大物，足足占了一整个房间。

33.en: Diels is trying to cut down the size and says that a laser around the size of a small table is in the offing.
parts: 迪尔斯正在设法缩小设备的体积。他说，一台只有小桌子那么大的激光器很快就会问世。

34.en: He plans to test this more manageable system on live thunderclouds next summer.
parts: 他计划明年夏天用真正带电的雷云测试这套更易操作的系统。

35.en: Bernstein says that Diels’s system is attracting lots of interest from the power companies.
parts: 伯恩斯坦说，迪尔斯的系统正引起电力公司的浓厚兴趣。

36.en: But they have not yet come up with the $5 million that EPRI says will be needed to develop a commercial system, by making the lasers yet smaller and cheaper.
parts: 但电力公司还没拿出这500万美元。电力研究所说，开发商用系统需要这笔钱，
以便把激光器做得更小、更便宜。

37.en: ‘I cannot say I have money yet, but I’m working on it,’ says Bernstein.
parts: “我目前还不能说钱已经到手，不过我正在想办法筹措，”伯恩斯坦说。
terms: 正在设法解决（筹款问题）

38.en: He reckons that the forthcoming field tests will be the turning point - and he’s hoping for good news.
parts: 他认为，即将进行的实地试验将是转折点。他希望得到好消息。

39.en: Bernstein predicts ‘an avalanche of interest and support’ if all goes well.
parts: 伯恩斯坦预计，如果一切顺利，“关注与支持将纷至沓来”。

40.en: He expects to see cloud-zappers eventually costing $50,000 to $100,000 each.
parts: 他预计，这种雷云放电装置最终每台需花费5万至10万美元。
其他科学家也可能从中受益。

42.en: With a lightning ‘switch’ at their fingertips, materials scientists could find out what happens when mighty currents meet matter.
parts: 如果有了随手就能操纵的闪电“开关”，材料科学家就能弄清强电流接触物质时会发生什么。

43.en: Diels also hopes to see the birth of ‘interactive meteorology’ - not just forecasting the weather but controlling it.
parts: 迪尔斯还希望看到“互动气象学”诞生，
不仅能预报天气，还能控制天气。

44.en: ‘If we could discharge clouds, we might affect the weather,’ he says.
parts: “如果我们能让云层放电，或许就能影响天气，”他说。

45.en: And perhaps, says Diels, we’ll be able to confront some other meteorological menaces.
parts: 迪尔斯说，或许我们还能应对其他一些气象威胁。

46.en: ‘We think we could prevent hail by inducing lightning,’ he says.
parts: 他说：“我们认为，通过引发闪电，也许可以防止下冰雹。”

47.en: Thunder, the shock wave that comes from a lightning flash, is thought to be the trigger for the torrential rain that is typical of storms.
parts: 雷声是闪电产生的冲击波。人们认为，它会引发暴风雨中常见的倾盆大雨。

49.en: With luck, as the storm clouds gather this winter, laser-toting researchers could, for the first time, strike back.
parts: 如果运气好，今年冬天雷雨云聚集时，携带激光设备的研究人员或许能首次展开反击。

22.en: According to Mrs Kaiser Jamil of RRL, ‘The Argentinian weevil does not attack any other plant and a pair of adult bugs could destroy the weed in 4-5 days.’
parts: 地区研究实验室的凯泽尔·贾米尔女士说，“这种阿根廷象鼻虫不会危害其他任何植物，一对象鼻虫成虫可能在四五天内就能毁掉这种杂草。”

23.en: CIBC is also perfecting the technique for breeding parasites that prey on ‘disapene scale’ insects - notorious defoliants of fruit trees in the US and India.
parts: 英联邦生物防治研究所也在改进一种技术，用于繁育捕食盾蚧的寄生性天敌。盾蚧是美国和印度出了名的果树害虫，能使果树落叶。

1.en: The continuous and reckless use of synthetic chemicals for the control of pests which pose a threat to agricultural crops and human health is proving to be counter-productive.
parts: 人们持续而不加节制地使用合成化学品来防治害虫。
这些害虫会威胁农作物和人类健康，而事实正表明，这样用药反而适得其反。

2.en: Apart from engendering widespread ecological disorders, pesticides have contributed to the emergence of a new breed of chemical-resistant, highly lethal superbugs.
parts: 杀虫剂除了引发大范围的生态失调，还促成了一类新害虫的出现：这些“超级害虫”对化学药剂有抗性，杀伤力极强。
terms: 此处指抗药性强的超级害虫

3.en: According to a recent study by the Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO), more than 300 species of agricultural pests have developed resistance to a wide range of potent chemicals.
parts: 据联合国粮食及农业组织近期的一项研究，已有三百多种农业害虫对多种强效化学药剂产生了抗性。
names: 联合国粮食及农业组织

4.en: Not to be left behind are the disease-spreading pests, about 100 species of which have become immune to a variety of insecticides now in use.
parts: 传播疾病的害虫也不例外：其中约有一百种已对目前使用的多种杀虫剂产生了抗性。

5.en: One glaring disadvantage of pesticides’ application is that, while destroying harmful pests, they also wipe out many useful non-targeted organisms, which keep the growth of the pest population in check.
parts: 施用农药有一个明显的弊端：在消灭害虫的同时，也会消灭许多本不在防治范围内的有益生物，而这些生物原本能抑制害虫种群增长。

6.en: This results in what agroecologists call the ‘treadmill syndrome’.
parts: 由此便出现了农业生态学家所说的“农药恶性循环”。
terms: 此处指越用农药越依赖用药的恶性循环

7.en: Because of their tremendous breeding potential and genetic diversity, many pests are known to withstand synthetic chemicals and bear offspring with a built-in resistance to pesticides.
parts: 由于害虫有着巨大的繁殖潜力和丰富的遗传多样性，
人们已知其中许多害虫能耐受合成化学药剂，还能繁衍出天生就对农药有抗性的后代。

8.en: The havoc that the ‘treadmill syndrome’ can bring about is well illustrated by what happened to cotton farmers in Central America.
parts: 中美洲棉农的经历清楚地说明了这种“农药恶性循环”会造成多么严重的破坏。

9.en: In the early 1940s, basking in the glory of chemical-based intensive agriculture, the farmers avidly took to pesticides as a sure measure to boost crop yield.
parts: 20世纪40年代初，棉农陶醉于依靠化学品的集约化农业所取得的成就，热衷于使用农药，把它看作提高作物产量的可靠办法。

10.en: The insecticide was applied eight times a year in the mid-1940s, rising to 28 in a season in the mid-1950s, following the sudden proliferation of three new varieties of chemical-resistant pests.
parts: 20世纪40年代中期，杀虫剂每年施用八次；到了50年代中期，用药次数升至每季二十八次，原因是三种新的抗药害虫突然大量繁殖。

11.en: By the mid-1960s, the situation took an alarming turn with the outbreak of four more new pests, necessitating pesticide spraying to such an extent that 50% of the financial outlay on cotton production was accounted for by pesticides.
parts: 到20世纪60年代中期，又有四种新的害虫暴发，情况急转直下，令人担忧。
棉农不得不大量喷洒农药，以至于棉花生产开支的一半都花在了农药上。

12.en: In the early 1970s, the spraying frequently reached 70 times a season as the farmers were pushed to the wall by the invasion of genetically stronger insect species.
parts: 20世纪70年代初，遗传上更有生存优势的昆虫种类入侵，把农户逼得走投无路，喷药次数常常达到每季七十次。

13.en: Most of the pesticides in the market today remain inadequately tested for properties that cause cancer and mutations as well as for other adverse effects on health, says a study by United States environmental agencies.
parts: 目前市面上的大多数农药，在致癌性和致突变性方面仍未得到充分检测，
对健康的其他不良影响也缺乏充分检测。美国环境机构的一项研究这样指出。

14.en: The United States National Resource Defense Council has found that DDT was the most popular of a long list of dangerous chemicals in use.
parts: 美国自然资源保护委员会发现，在当时使用的众多危险化学品中，滴滴涕最为常用。
names: 美国自然资源保护委员会

15.en: In the face of the escalating perils from indiscriminate applications of pesticides, a more effective and ecologically sound strategy of biological control, involving the selective use of natural enemies of the pest population, is fast gaining popularity-though, as yet, it is a new field with limited potential.
parts: 面对不加节制地施用农药所带来的日益严重的危险，有一种更有效、在生态上也更合理的生物防治策略，
它有选择地利用害虫的天敌，正迅速受到青睐。不过，这仍是一个潜力有限的新领域。

16.en: The advantage of biological control in contrast to other methods is that it provides a relatively low-cost, perpetual control system with a minimum of detrimental side-effects.
parts: 与其他方法相比，生物防治的优势在于，它能以较低成本提供持续发挥作用的防治体系，并把有害副作用降到很低。

17.en: When handled by experts, bio-control is safe, non-polluting and self-dispersing.
parts: 由专家实施时，生物防治是安全的，不造成污染，而且防治生物能自行扩散。

18.en: The Commonwealth Institute of Biological Control (CIBC) in Bangalore, with its global network of research laboratories and field stations, is one of the most active, non-commercial research agencies engaged in pest control by setting natural predators against parasites.
parts: 设在班加罗尔的英联邦生物防治研究所在全球拥有研究实验室和野外工作站。
它是最活跃的非商业性研究机构之一，利用天然捕食者对付寄生生物，借此防治害虫。
names: 英联邦生物防治研究所

19.en: CIBC also serves as a clearing-house for the export and import of biological agents for pest control world-wide.
parts: 该研究所还充当全球协调中心，协调各地防治害虫所用生物的进出口。

20.en: CIBC successfully used a seed-feeding weevil, native to Mexico, to control the obnoxious parthenium weed, known to exert devious influence on agriculture and human health in both India and Australia.
parts: 英联邦生物防治研究所曾成功利用一种原产于墨西哥、以种子为食的象鼻虫，防治有害杂草银胶菊。
人们知道，这种杂草会以不易察觉的方式危害印度和澳大利亚的农业及人类健康。

21.en: Similarly the Hyderabad-based Regional Research Laboratory (RRL), supported by CIBC, is now trying out an Argentinian weevil for the eradication of water hyacinth, another dangerous weed, which has become a nuisance in many parts of the world.
parts: 同样，在英联邦生物防治研究所的支持下，位于海得拉巴的地区研究实验室正试用一种阿根廷象鼻虫来根除水葫芦。
水葫芦是另一种危险杂草，已在世界许多地方成为一大祸患。

24.en: How effectively biological control can be pressed into service is proved by the following examples.
parts: 下面的例子表明，生物防治付诸实际应用时能有多大成效。

25.en: In the late 1960s, when Sri Lanka’s flourishing coconut groves were plagued by leaf-mining hispides, a larval parasite imported from Singapore brought the pest under control.
parts: 20世纪60年代末，斯里兰卡茂盛的椰林受到潜叶铁甲虫的严重侵害。人们从新加坡引入了一种寄生于害虫幼虫的天敌，控制住了虫害。

26.en: A natural predator indigenous to India, Neodumetia sangawani, was found useful in controlling the Rhodes grass-scale insect that was devouring forage grass in many parts of the US.
parts: 研究发现，原产于印度的一种天敌（Neodumetia sangawani）有助于防治罗德草蚧；这种介壳虫当时正在美国许多地区大量啃食牧草。

27.en: By using Neochetina bruci, a beetle native to Brazil, scientists at Kerala Agricultural University freed a 12-kilometre-long canal from the clutches of the weed Salvinia molesta, popularly called ‘African Payal’ in Kerala.
parts: 借助一种原产于巴西的甲虫（Neochetina bruci），
喀拉拉农业大学的科学家使一条十二公里长的运河摆脱了有害槐叶萍（Salvinia molesta）的侵害；
这种杂草在喀拉拉当地俗称“非洲帕亚尔”。
terms: 从……的控制中；摆脱……的侵害

28.en: About 30,000 hectares of rice fields in Kerala are infested by this weed.
parts: 在喀拉拉，约有三万公顷稻田受到这种杂草的侵害。

4.en: A brain that can do this is an iconoclastic one.
parts: 有这种能力的大脑，能够打破思维常规。

9.en: But the field of neuroeconomics was born out of the realization that the physical workings of the brain place limitations on the way we make decisions.
parts: 不过，神经经济学之所以出现，是因为人们认识到，大脑的生理运作机制制约着我们作决策的方式。

10.en: By understanding these constraints, we begin to understand why some people march to a different drumbeat.
parts: 了解了这些限制，我们便开始明白，为什么有些人会按自己的方式行事。

13.en: This is where most people are impeded from being an iconoclast.
parts: 正是这一点，使大多数人很难成为打破常规的人。

16.en: This happens all the time.
parts: 这种情况随时都在发生。

20.en: More than the physical reality of photons or sound waves, perception is a product of the brain.
parts: 相比于光子或声波这些物理现象，知觉更多地是大脑活动的产物。

24.en: Iconoclasts, either because they were born that way or through learning, have found ways to work around the perceptual shortcuts that plague most people.
parts: 打破常规的人，或是天生如此，或是经后天学习，已经找到了绕开那些困扰多数人的知觉捷径的办法。

25.en: Perception is not something that is hardwired into the brain.
parts: 知觉并非大脑与生俱来便已设定好的东西。

28.en: Everything the brain sees, hears, or touches has multiple interpretations.
parts: 无论大脑看到、听到还是触碰到什么，都有不止一种解释。

30.en: In technical terms, these conjectures have their basis in the statistical likelihood of one interpretation over another and are heavily influenced by past experience and, importantly for potential iconoclasts, what other people say.
parts: 从技术上说，这些推测的依据是，从统计角度看，某一种解释比另一种更有可能成立。
过去的经验会对这些推测产生很大影响。别人的话同样有很大影响，这一点对可能打破常规的人尤其重要。

32.en: Novelty releases the perceptual process from the chains of past experience and forces the brain to make new judgments.
parts: 新事物使知觉过程摆脱过往经验的束缚，并迫使大脑作出新的判断。

39.en: But fear of public speaking, which everyone must do from time to time, afflicts one-third of the population.
parts: 然而，人人都不时需要当众讲话，而对当众讲话的恐惧却困扰着三分之一的人。

40.en: This makes it too common to be considered a mental disorder.
parts: 这种恐惧太普遍了，因而不能算作一种精神障碍。

42.en: Finally, to be successful iconoclasts, individuals must sell their ideas to other people.
parts: 最后，要成为成功的破格创新者，还必须说服别人接受自己的想法。
terms: 说服别人接受自己的想法

45.en: In the last decade there has been an explosion of knowledge about the social brain and how the brain works when groups coordinate decision making.
parts: 过去十年，人们对社会脑的认识迅速增长，
也越来越了解群体协调决策时大脑如何运作。

46.en: Neuroscience has revealed which brain circuits are responsible for functions like understanding what other people think, empathy, fairness, and social identity.
parts: 神经科学已经揭示，理解他人的想法、共情、公平感和社会认同等功能分别由哪些脑回路负责。

52.en: They supply creativity and innovation not easily accomplished by committees.
parts: 他们能贡献创造力，推动创新，而这些往往是委员会难以做到的。

55.en: It is crucial for success in any field to understand how the iconoclastic mind works.
parts: 要在任何领域取得成功，了解善于打破常规的人如何思考都至关重要。

29.en: The one that is ultimately chosen is simply the brain’s best theory.
parts: 最终选定的那种解释，不过是大脑认为最说得通的一种推测。

8.en: It was only after the creation of the FAA that full-scale regulation of America’s airspace took place, and this was fortuitous, for the advent of the jet engine suddenly resulted in a large number of very fast planes, reducing pilots’ margin of error and practically demanding some set of rules to keep everyone well separated and operating safely in the air.
parts: 直到美国联邦航空管理局成立之后，美国才开始对本国空域实施全面管制。这个时机恰好合适，
因为喷气发动机的问世一下子带来了大批飞行速度极快的飞机，
使飞行员出错的余地变小，几乎非得订出一套规则，让各架飞机保持足够的间隔，在空中安全飞行。

11.en: The FAA realised that the airspace over the United States would at any time have many different kinds of planes, flying for many different purposes, in a variety of weather conditions, and the same kind of structure was needed to accommodate all of them.
parts: 美国联邦航空管理局意识到，在任何时候，美国上空都会有多种飞机，
它们的飞行目的各不相同，遇到的天气条件也各不相同，
因此需要一套统一的空域管理体系，兼顾所有这些情况。

18.en: In this way, the recreational pilot who simply wishes to go flying for a while without all the restrictions imposed by the FAA has only to stay in uncontrolled airspace, below 365m, while the pilot who does want the protection afforded by ATC can easily enter the controlled airspace.
parts: 这样，休闲飞行员如果只想飞上一会儿，不想受联邦航空管理局种种限制的约束，只需留在365米以下的非管制空域。
而希望得到空中交通管制保护的飞行员，则可很方便地进入管制空域。

22.en: On a clear day, a pilot in controlled airspace can choose a VFR or IFR flight plan, and the FAA regulations were devised in a way which accommodates both VFR and IFR operations in the same airspace.
parts: 在晴朗的日子里，管制空域内的飞行员可以选择按目视飞行规则或仪表飞行规则制订飞行计划。
联邦航空管理局在制定规章时作了相应安排，使这两类飞行能够在同一空域内进行。

28.en: Generally, Class E airspace is where one finds general aviation aircraft (few of which can climb above 5,490m anyway), and commercial turboprop aircraft.
parts: 一般来说，在E类空域飞行的是通用航空飞机（反正其中很少有能爬升到5490米以上的），以及商用涡轮螺旋桨飞机。

25.en: Uncontrolled airspace is designated Class F, while controlled airspace below 5,490m above sea level and not in the vicinity of an airport is Class E.
parts: 非管制空域定为F类，而海拔低于5,490米且不在机场附近的管制空域则属E类。

26.en: All airspace above 5,490m is designated Class A.
parts: 海拔高于5,490米的空域一律划为A类。

27.en: The reason for the division of Class E and Class A airspace stems from the type of planes operating in them.
parts: 将空域分为E类和A类，原因在于两类空域中飞行的飞机类型不同。

1.en: An accident that occurred in the skies over the Grand Canyon in 1956 resulted in the establishment of the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) to regulate and oversee the operation of aircraft in the skies over the United States, which were becoming quite congested.
parts: 1956年，大峡谷上空发生的一起事故促成了美国联邦航空管理局（FAA）的成立。
该机构负责规范和监督航空器在美国上空的运行，当时这片空域正变得相当拥挤。

4.en: As early as the 1920s, the earliest air traffic controllers manually guided aircraft in the vicinity of the airports, using lights and flags, while beacons and flashing lights were placed along cross-country routes to establish the earliest airways.
parts: 早在20世纪20年代，第一批空中交通管制员就用灯光和旗帜，以人工方式引导机场附近的飞机。
与此同时，人们沿国内长途飞行路线设置信标和闪光灯，建起了最早的空中航路。
terms: 横跨国内的长途飞行路线

10.en: AIS scientists work across a number of sports, applying skills learned in one - such as building muscle strength in golfers - to others, such as swimming and squash.
parts: 澳大利亚体育学院的科学家跨多个运动项目开展研究，把在某一项目中学到的技巧——例如增强高尔夫球手肌肉力量的方法——应用到其他项目中，例如游泳和壁球。

5.en: At the Australian Institute of Sport (AIS), hundreds of youngsters and pros live and train under the eyes of coaches.
parts: 在澳大利亚体育学院（AIS），数百名年轻运动员和职业选手在教练的注视下生活、训练。

9.en: The AIS employs more than 100 sports scientists and doctors, and collaborates with scores of others in universities and research centres.
parts: 澳大利亚体育学院聘用了100多名运动科学家和医生，还与大学和研究中心的许多其他专家合作。

13.en: ‘We can’t waste our time looking at ethereal scientific questions that don’t help the coach work with an athlete and improve performance,’ says Peter Fricker, chief of science at AIS.
parts: “我们不能把时间浪费在那些虚无缥缈、对教练指导运动员提高成绩毫无帮助的科学问题上。”
澳大利亚体育学院科研负责人彼得·弗里克说。

19.en: To demonstrate how the system works, Bruce Mason at AIS shows off the prototype of a 3D analysis tool for studying swimmers.
parts: 为了演示这套系统如何运作，澳大利亚体育学院的布鲁斯·梅森展示了一款用于研究游泳运动员的三维分析工具的原型。

21.en: Looking side-on, Mason measures the distance between strokes.
parts: 梅森从侧面测量这名运动员每次划水前进的距离。
terms: 两次划水之间前进的距离

24.en: Mason’s contribution to sport also includes the development of the SWAN (Swimming Analysis) system now used in Australian national competitions.
parts: 梅森对体育的贡献还包括开发SWAN（游泳分析）系统，现在澳大利亚的全国性比赛正在使用这套系统。

27.en: ‘Take a look,’ says Mason, pulling out a sheet of data.
parts: “看一下。”梅森边说边拿出一张数据表。

29.en: So why did he finish 35 hundredths of a second down?
parts: 那么，他为什么落后了0.35秒才到终点？

30.en: ‘His turn times were 44 hundredths of a second behind the other guy,’ says Mason.
parts: “他转身用的时间比另一名选手多了0.44秒。”梅森说。

32.en: This is the kind of accuracy that AIS scientists’ research is bringing to a range of sports.
parts: 这正是澳大利亚体育学院科学家的研究给多个运动项目带来的精确程度。

36.en: After years of experimentation, AIS and the University of Newcastle in New South Wales developed a test that measures how much of the immune-system protein immunoglobulin A is present in athletes’ saliva.
parts: 经过多年实验，澳大利亚体育学院与新南威尔士州的纽卡斯尔大学共同开发了一项检测，
可以测出运动员唾液中一种免疫系统蛋白质——免疫球蛋白A的含量。

39.en: Since the tests were introduced, AIS athletes in all sports have been remarkably successful at staying healthy.
parts: 自实施这些检测以来，澳大利亚体育学院各运动项目的运动员在保持健康方面成效显著。

42.en: ‘You design the model to make that time,’ says Mason.
parts: 梅森说：“设计这一模型，为的是让运动员游出那个目标时间。”

47.en: Some years ago, the AIS unveiled coolant-lined jackets for endurance athletes.
parts: 几年前，澳大利亚体育学院为耐力项目的运动员推出了衬有冷却材料的夹克。

50.en: The same has happened to the ‘altitude tent’, developed by AIS to replicate the effect of altitude training at sea level.
parts: 澳大利亚体育学院研制的“高原帐篷”也经历了同样的过程；它能在海平面高度模拟高原训练的效果。

4.en: A big part of the secret is an extensive and expensive network of sporting academies underpinned by science and medicine.
parts: 秘诀很大程度上在于一个覆盖面广、耗资不菲的体育学院网络，背后有科学和医学作支撑。

33.en: With the Cooperative Research Centre for Micro Technology in Melbourne, they are developing unobtrusive sensors that will be embedded in an athlete’s clothes or running shoes to monitor heart rate, sweating, heat production or any other factor that might have an impact on an athlete’s ability to run.
parts: 他们正与墨尔本的微技术合作研究中心共同开发不引人注意的传感器。
这些传感器将嵌入运动员的衣服或跑鞋，
监测心率、出汗、产热，以及任何可能影响运动员跑步能力的其他因素。

46.en: Of course, there’s nothing to stop other countries copying – and many have tried.
parts: 当然，其他国家也完全可以仿效，许多国家已经尝试过。

51.en: But Australia’s success story is about more than easily copied technological fixes, and up to now no nation has replicated its all-encompassing system.
parts: 但澳大利亚的成功不能单靠那些容易模仿的技术手段来解释；迄今还没有哪个国家复制出它这套包罗各方面的体系。

25.en: It collects images from digital cameras running at 50 frames a second and breaks down each part of a swimmer’s performance into factors that can be analysed individually - stroke length, stroke frequency, average duration of each stroke, velocity, start, lap and finish times, and so on.
parts: 这套系统从每秒拍摄50帧的数码摄像机中获取图像，
把运动员游泳表现的各个环节分解为可单独分析的指标，
例如划距、划频、每次划水的平均用时、游速，以及出发、各分段和终点的计时等。

10.en: Clearly, Japanese carpenters of the day knew a few tricks about allowing a building to sway and settle itself rather than fight nature’s forces.
parts: 显然，当时的日本木匠掌握了一些窍门，能让建筑物随之摇摆、再自行恢复稳定，避免与自然力硬抗。

1.en: In a land swept by typhoons and shaken by earthquakes, how have Japan’s tallest and seemingly flimsiest old buildings - 500 or so wooden pagodas - remained standing for centuries?
parts: 日本常遭台风侵袭和地震撼动。
在这片土地上，那些最高、看似最不牢靠的古建筑——约五百座木塔——为何能屹立数百年？

2.en: Records show that only two have collapsed during the past 1400 years.
parts: 记录显示，过去一千四百年间，只有两座塔倒塌。

3.en: Those that have disappeared were destroyed by fire as a result of lightning or civil war.
parts: 那些已经不复存在的塔，是毁于雷击或内战引起的火灾。

4.en: The disastrous Hanshin earthquake in 1995 killed 6,400 people, toppled elevated highways, flattened office blocks and devastated the port area of Kobe.
parts: 1995年的阪神大地震造成6400人死亡，高架公路倾塌，办公楼被夷为平地，神户港区也遭到严重破坏。

5.en: Yet it left the magnificent five-storey pagoda at the Toji temple in nearby Kyoto unscathed, though it levelled a number of buildings in the neighbourhood.
parts: 然而，附近京都东寺那座宏伟的五层塔却在地震中毫发无损，尽管周围好些建筑都被夷为平地。

6.en: Japanese scholars have been mystified for ages about why these tall, slender buildings are so stable.
parts: 长期以来，日本学者一直不明白，这些高而细长的建筑为何如此稳固。

7.en: It was only thirty years ago that the building industry felt confident enough to erect office blocks of steel and reinforced concrete that had more than a dozen floors.
parts: 直到三十年前，建筑业才有足够的信心，用钢材和钢筋混凝土建造超过十二层的办公楼。

8.en: With its special shock absorbers to dampen the effect of sudden sideways movements from an earthquake, the thirty-six-storey Kasumigaseki building in central Tokyo - Japan’s first skyscraper - was considered a masterpiece of modern engineering when it was built in 1968.
parts: 专门的减震器可以减轻地震引起的突发横向运动的影响。
配有这种装置的霞关大厦位于东京市中心，高三十六层，是日本第一座摩天楼。它在1968年建成时被视为现代工程的杰作。

9.en: Yet in 826, with only pegs and wedges to keep his wooden structure upright, the master builder Kobodaishi had no hesitation in sending his majestic Toji pagoda soaring fifty-five metres into the sky - nearly half as high as the Kasumigaseki skyscraper built some eleven centuries later.
parts: 然而早在826年，仅靠木销和楔子保持木结构直立，
建筑名匠弘法大师就毫不犹豫地建起了高五十五米、巍然耸立的东寺塔。
它的高度接近约一千一百年后建成的霞关大厦的一半。

11.en: But what sort of tricks?
parts: 可到底是什么窍门呢？

12.en: The multi-storey pagoda came to Japan from China in the sixth century.
parts: 六世纪，多层佛塔从中国传入日本。

13.en: As in China, they were first introduced with Buddhism and were attached to important temples.
parts: 与中国的情况一样，这些塔最初随佛教传入，附属于重要的寺院。

14.en: The Chinese built their pagodas in brick or stone, with inner staircases, and used them in later centuries mainly as watchtowers.
parts: 中国人用砖或石材建塔，塔内设有楼梯；在后来的几个世纪里，这些塔主要用作瞭望塔。

15.en: When the pagoda reached Japan, however, its architecture was freely adapted to local conditions - they were built less high, typically five rather than nine storeys, made mainly of wood and the staircase was dispensed with because the Japanese pagoda did not have any practical use but became more of an art object.
parts: 然而，佛塔传到日本后，建筑形式因地制宜，有了大幅调整。
日本佛塔造得较矮，通常为五层而非九层，主要用木材建造，楼梯也被省去了。
这是因为日本佛塔没有实际用途，更像是一件艺术品。

16.en: Because of the typhoons that batter Japan in the summer, Japanese builders learned to extend the eaves of buildings further beyond the walls.
parts: 由于日本夏季常遭台风猛袭，当地工匠学会了把屋檐向墙外伸得更远。

17.en: This prevents rainwater gushing down the walls.
parts: 这样可以防止雨水沿着墙面急流而下。

18.en: Pagodas in China and Korea have nothing like the overhang that is found on pagodas in Japan.
parts: 中国和韩国的佛塔，屋檐都远没有日本佛塔挑出得那么长。

19.en: The roof of a Japanese temple building can be made to overhang the sides of the structure by fifty per cent or more of the building’s overall width.
parts: 日本寺院建筑的屋顶可从侧面向外挑出，距离可达建筑总宽度的一半或更多。

20.en: For the same reason, the builders of Japanese pagodas seem to have further increased their weight by choosing to cover these extended eaves not with the porcelain tiles of many Chinese pagodas but with much heavier earthenware tiles.
parts: 出于同样的原因，建造日本佛塔的工匠似乎还让塔更重了。
他们选择在这些挑出的屋檐上铺设比瓷瓦重得多的陶瓦；许多中国佛塔用的则是瓷瓦。

21.en: But this does not totally explain the great resilience of Japanese pagodas.
parts: 但这还不能完全解释日本佛塔为何如此经得住冲击。
terms: 承受冲击并恢复的能力

22.en: Is the answer that, like a tall pine tree, the Japanese pagoda - with its massive trunk-like central pillar known as shinbashira - simply flexes and sways during a typhoon or earthquake?
parts: 答案会不会是这样：日本佛塔像一棵高大的松树，有一根树干般粗壮的中央立柱，称为“心柱”，
在台风或地震中只是弯曲、摇摆？

23.en: For centuries, many thought so.
parts: 几个世纪以来，许多人都是这样认为的。

24.en: But the answer is not so simple because the startling thing is that the shinbashira actually carries no load at all.
parts: 但答案没这么简单。令人意外的是，心柱实际上完全不承重。

25.en: In fact, in some pagoda designs, it does not even rest on the ground, but is suspended from the top of the pagoda - hanging loosely down through the middle of the building.
parts: 事实上，有些佛塔的心柱甚至不落地，而是悬挂在塔顶，
从那里垂下，自由地穿过整座塔的中央。

26.en: The weight of the building is supported entirely by twelve outer and four inner columns.
parts: 整座塔的重量完全由十二根外柱和四根内柱支撑。

27.en: And what is the role of the shinbashira, the central pillar?
parts: 那么，居中的这根心柱究竟起什么作用？

28.en: The best way to understand the shinbashira’s role is to watch a video made by Shuzo Ishida, a structural engineer at Kyoto Institute of Technology.
parts: 要了解心柱的作用，最好看一段由京都工艺纤维大学结构工程师石田修三拍摄的视频。

29.en: Mr. Ishida, known to his students as ‘Professor Pagoda’ because of his passion to understand the pagoda, has built a series of models and tested them on a ‘shake-table’ in his laboratory.
parts: 石田先生热衷于研究佛塔，学生们称他为“佛塔教授”。
他制作了一系列模型，在实验室的振动台上进行测试。

30.en: In short, the shinbashira was acting like an enormous stationary pendulum.
parts: 简而言之，心柱起到了一个巨大静止摆锤的作用。

31.en: The ancient craftsmen, apparently without the assistance of very advanced mathematics, seemed to grasp the principles that were, more than a thousand years later, applied in the construction of Japan’s first skyscraper.
parts: 古代工匠看来并未借助十分高深的数学，却似乎已经掌握了一些原理。
一千多年后，人们把这些原理用于建造日本的第一座摩天楼。

32.en: What those early craftsmen had found by trial and error was that under pressure a pagoda’s loose stack of floors could be made to slither to and fro independent of one another.
parts: 那些早期工匠经过反复试验发现，
塔身受力时，松松叠在一起的各层可以彼此独立地来回滑动。

33.en: Viewed from the side, the pagoda seemed to be doing a snake dance - with each consecutive floor moving in the opposite direction to its neighbours above and below.
parts: 从侧面看，塔仿佛在跳蛇舞，每一层都朝着与其上下相邻楼层相反的方向移动。

34.en: The shinbashira, running up through a hole in the centre of the building, constrained individual storeys from moving too far because, after moving a certain distance, they banged into it, transmitting energy away along the column.
parts: 心柱从建筑中央的孔洞中向上贯穿，限制各层的移动幅度。
这是因为每一层移到一定距离后便会碰到心柱，能量便沿着柱子传走。

35.en: Another strange feature of the Japanese pagoda is that, because the building tapers, with each successive floor plan being smaller than the one below, none of the vertical pillars that carry the weight of the building is connected to its corresponding pillar above.
parts: 日本佛塔还有一个奇特之处。由于塔身向上逐渐收窄，每层的平面都比下一层小，
承重的竖柱没有一根与上层对应的柱子相连。

36.en: In other words, a five-storey pagoda contains not even one pillar that travels right up through the building to carry the structural loads from the top to the bottom.
parts: 换句话说，在一座五层佛塔里，连一根从顶到底贯通全塔、把上部结构荷载传到塔底的柱子都没有。
terms: from the top to the bottom
from the top to the bottom

37.en: More surprising is the fact that the individual storeys of a Japanese pagoda, unlike their counterparts elsewhere, are not actually connected to each other.
parts: 更令人惊讶的是，日本佛塔各层之间实际上互不相连，这和其他地方的同类佛塔不同。

38.en: They are simply stacked one on top of another like a pile of hats.
parts: 各层只是一个叠一个地摞着，就像一摞帽子。

39.en: Interestingly, such a design would not be permitted under current Japanese building regulations.
parts: 有意思的是，按照日本现行的建筑法规，这样的设计不会获准采用。

40.en: And the extra-wide eaves?
parts: 那格外宽大的屋檐又有什么作用？

41.en: Think of them as a tightrope walker’s balancing pole.
parts: 可以把这些屋檐想象成走钢丝者手中的平衡杆。

42.en: The bigger the mass at each end of the pole, the easier it is for the tightrope walker to maintain his or her balance.
parts: 平衡杆两端的质量越大，走钢丝的人就越容易保持平衡。

43.en: The same holds true for a pagoda.
parts: 同样的道理也适用于佛塔。

44.en: ‘With the eaves extending out on all sides like balancing poles,’ says Mr Ishida, ‘the building responds to even the most powerful jolt of an earthquake with a graceful swaying, never an abrupt shaking.’
parts: “屋檐像平衡杆一样向四面伸出，”石田先生说，
“哪怕地震带来最猛烈的冲击，塔身也会舒缓地摇摆，绝不会猛地一晃。”

45.en: Here again, Japanese master builders of a thousand years ago anticipated concepts of modern structural engineering.
parts: 这也表明，现代结构工程的某些理念，日本的建筑名匠在一千年前就已想到。

18.en: The ancient Gothic word for ten, tachund, is used to express the number 100 as tachund tachund.
parts: 古哥特语中表示“十”的词是 tachund，表示“一百”时就把这个词连用两次，写成 tachund tachund。
terms: 古哥特语中表示“一百”的说法

19.en: By the seventh century, the word teon had become interchangeable with the tachund or hund of the Anglo-Saxon language, and so 100 was denoted as hund teontig, or ten times ten.
parts: 到了七世纪，teon 已可与盎格鲁-撒克逊语中的 tachund 或 hund 互换使用，
因此一百便写作 hund teontig，意思是十乘以十。

1.en: One of the first great intellectual feats of a young child is learning how to talk, closely followed by learning how to count.
parts: 幼儿最早取得的一项重要智力成就是学会说话，紧接着便是学会数数。

2.en: From earliest childhood we are so bound up with our system of numeration that it is a feat of imagination to consider the problems faced by early humans who had not yet developed this facility.
parts: 我们从很小的时候起就与计数体系密不可分，
要设想早期人类在尚未具备这种能力时所遇到的困难，得有相当的想象力。

3.en: Careful consideration of our system of numeration leads to the conviction that, rather than being a facility that comes naturally to a person, it is one of the great and remarkable achievements of the human race.
parts: 仔细审视我们的计数体系就会确信，
计数并非人与生俱来的能力，而是人类伟大而非凡的成就之一。

4.en: It is impossible to learn the sequence of events that led to our developing the concept of number.
parts: 我们无从知道，人类究竟经历了怎样一连串事件，才形成了数的概念。

5.en: Even the earliest of tribes had a system of numeration that, if not advanced, was sufficient for the tasks that they had to perform.
parts: 即使是最早的部落也有自己的计数体系。它即便谈不上先进，也足以应付当时必须做的事。

6.en: Our ancestors had little use for actual numbers; instead their considerations would have been more of the kind Is this enough? rather than How many?
parts: 我们的祖先很少用得上具体的数目。他们考虑的想必更多是「这些够不够」，而非「有多少」。

7.en: When they were engaged in food gathering, for example.
parts: 例如，他们采集食物时就是如此。

8.en: However, when early humans first began to reflect on the nature of things around them, they discovered that they needed an idea of number simply to keep their thoughts in order.
parts: 然而，早期人类最初开始思考周围事物的本质时，他们发现，哪怕只是为了理清思路，也需要有数的概念。

9.en: As they began to settle, grow plants and herd animals, the need for a sophisticated number system became paramount.
parts: 当人类开始定居、种植作物和放牧牲畜时，拥有一套较为复杂的计数体系就变得至关重要。

10.en: It will never be known how and when this numeration ability developed, but it is certain that numeration was well developed by the time humans had formed even semi-permanent settlements.
parts: 这种计数能力是怎样、又是在何时形成的，我们永远无从得知。
但有一点可以肯定：早在人类形成哪怕只是半永久性的定居点时，计数就已相当发达。

11.en: Evidence of early stages of arithmetic and numeration can be readily found.
parts: 算术和计数法早期发展阶段的证据很容易找到。

12.en: The indigenous peoples of Tasmania were only able to count one, two, many; those of South Africa counted one, two, two and one, two twos, two twos and one, and so on.
parts: 塔斯马尼亚的原住民只能数「一、二、许多」。
南非的原住民则数「一、二、二加一、两个二、两个二加一」，以此类推。

13.en: But in real situations the number and words are often accompanied by gestures to help resolve any confusion.
parts: 但在实际情境中，人们报数或说出相应词语时，往往还会配上手势，帮助消除可能的歧义。

14.en: For example, when using the one, two, many type of system, the word many would mean, Look at my hands and see how many fingers I am showing you.
parts: 例如，在使用「一、二、许多」这类体系时，「许多」这个词的意思是「看看我的手，看看我向你伸出了几根手指」。

15.en: This basic approach is limited in the range of numbers that it can express, but this range will generally suffice when dealing with the simpler aspects of human existence.
parts: 这一基本方法所能表示的数目范围有限，
但应付人类生活中比较简单的事情，这个范围通常就够了。

16.en: The lack of ability of some cultures to deal with large numbers is not really surprising.
parts: 有些文化缺乏处理大数的能力，这其实并不奇怪。

17.en: European languages, when traced back to their earlier version, are very poor in number words and expressions.
parts: 回溯欧洲各语言早期的形态，会发现其中表示数的词语和说法非常有限。

20.en: The average person in the seventh century in Europe was not as familiar with numbers as we are today.
parts: 七世纪时，欧洲普通人对数的熟悉程度不及今天的我们。

21.en: In fact, to qualify as a witness in a court of law a man had to be able to count to nine!
parts: 事实上，当时一个人得能够数到九，才有资格在法庭上作证！

22.en: Perhaps the most fundamental step in developing a sense of number is not the ability to count, but rather to see that a number is really an abstract idea instead of a simple attachment to a group of particular objects.
parts: 形成数感最根本的一步，也许不在于能够数数，
而在于认识到数其实是一个抽象概念，并不只是附属于某一组具体事物的特征。

23.en: It must have been within the grasp of the earliest humans to conceive that four birds are distinct from two birds; however, it is not an elementary step to associate the number 4, as connected with four birds, to the number 4, as connected with four rocks.
parts: 最早的人类想必也能明白，四只鸟跟两只鸟是有区别的。
但要把四只鸟所对应的「四」与四块石头所对应的「四」联系在一起，却不是简单的一步。

24.en: Associating a number as one of the qualities of a specific object is a great hindrance to the development of a true number sense.
parts: 把数当作某个具体物体本身的一种属性，会严重妨碍真正数感的形成。

25.en: When the number 4 can be registered in the mind as a specific word, independent of the object being referenced, the individual is ready to take the first step toward the development of a notational system for numbers and, from there, to arithmetic.
parts: 当一个人能把「四」作为特定的词记在脑中，使它独立于所指的物体时，
他就具备了迈出第一步的条件，可以开始建立记录数的符号体系，再由此走向算术。

26.en: Traces of the very first stages in the development of numeration can be seen in several living languages today.
parts: 如今，在几种仍有人使用的语言中，还能看到计数法最初发展阶段留下的痕迹。

27.en: The numeration system of the Tsimshian language in British Columbia contains seven distinct sets of words for numbers according to the class of the item being counted: for counting flat objects and animals, for round objects and time, for people, for long objects and trees, for canoes, for measures, and for counting when no particular object is being numerated.
parts: 在不列颠哥伦比亚省的钦西安语中，数词按所数对象的类别分为七套：
一套数扁平物体和动物，一套数圆形物体和时间，一套数人，一套数长条物体和树木，
一套数独木舟，一套用于度量，最后一套用于单纯数数而不特指任何东西。

28.en: It seems that the last is a later development while the first six groups show the relics of an older system.
parts: 最后这一套似乎出现得较晚，前六套则保留着更早一种体系的痕迹。

29.en: This diversity of number names can also be found in some widely used languages such as Japanese.
parts: 在一些使用广泛的语言中，如日语，也能看到这种数词名称上的多样性。

30.en: Intermixed with the development of a number sense is the development of an ability to count.
parts: 数感的发展与数数能力的发展相互交织。

31.en: Counting is not directly related to the formation of a number concept because it is possible to count by matching the items being counted against a group of pebbles, grains of corn, or the counter’s fingers.
parts: 会数数与形成数的概念之间没有直接关联。
因为人们可以把要数的东西跟一堆小石子、玉米粒或数数者的手指一一对应，由此数出数量。

32.en: These aids would have been indispensable to very early people who would have found the process impossible without some form of mechanical aid.
parts: 这些辅助物对于远古人类想必不可或缺；倘若没有某种实物辅助，他们恐怕就无法完成计数。

33.en: Such aids, while different, are still used even by the most educated in today’s society due to their convenience.
parts: 今天，这类辅助工具虽然形式有所不同，但由于用起来方便，即便是社会上受教育程度最高的人也仍在使用。

34.en: All counting ultimately involves reference to something other than the things being counted.
parts: 说到底，任何计数都要借助所数对象之外的事物作为参照。

35.en: At first it may have been grains or pebbles but now it is a memorised sequence of words that happen to be the names of the numbers.
parts: 起初，用作参照的也许是谷粒或小石子，如今则是一串熟记在心的词，而这些词正好就是各个数的名称。

42.en: In America the period of huge productivity gains in transportation may be almost over, but in most countries the process still has far to go.
parts: 在美国，运输业生产率大幅提高的时期也许已接近尾声，但在大多数国家，这一进程还有很长的路要走。

43.en: State ownership of railways and airlines, regulation of freight rates and toleration of anti-competitive practices, such as cargo-handling monopolies, all keep the cost of shipping unnecessarily high and deter international trade.
parts: 铁路和航空公司归国家所有，运价受到管制，货物装卸被垄断等妨碍竞争的做法也受到容忍。
这些因素都使运输成本居高不下，妨碍了国际贸易。

32.en: The invention of the container crane made it possible to load and unload containers without capsizing the ship and the adoption of standard container sizes allowed almost any box to be transported on any ship.
parts: 集装箱起重机的发明使人们可以装卸集装箱而不致使船倾覆。
集装箱尺寸统一后，几乎任何一个箱子都能由任何一艘船运送。

4.en: Foreign products, from meat to machinery, play a more important role in almost every economy in the world, and foreign markets now tempt businesses that never much worried about sales beyond their nation’s borders.
parts: 从肉类到机械，外国产品在世界上几乎每个经济体中都比过去更重要了。
过去很少关心境外销售的企业，如今也受到海外市场的吸引。

12.en: Cheap labour may make Chinese clothing competitive in America, but if delays in shipment tie up working capital and cause winter coats to arrive in spring, trade may lose its advantages.
parts: 低廉的劳动力成本也许能让中国服装在美国市场上有竞争力，
但如果货运延误占压了流动资金，直到春天冬衣才到货，贸易的优势也可能随之消失。

13.en: At the turn of the 20th century, agriculture and manufacturing were the two most important sectors almost everywhere, accounting for about 70% of total output in Germany, Italy and France, and 40-50% in America, Britain and Japan.
parts: 在20世纪初，农业和制造业几乎在所有地方都是最重要的两个产业。
在德国、意大利和法国，两者约占总产出的70%，在美国、英国和日本则占40%至50%。
terms: At the turn of the 20th century
at the turn of the 20th century

14.en: International commerce was therefore dominated by raw materials, such as wheat, wood and iron ore, or processed commodities, such as meat and steel.
parts: 因此，国际贸易以原材料或加工商品为主。前者有小麦、木材、铁矿石，后者有肉类和钢材。

18.en: Today, it is finished manufactured products that dominate the flow of trade, and, thanks to technological advances such as lightweight components, manufactured goods themselves have tended to become lighter and less bulky.
parts: 如今，主导贸易的是制成品。
而轻型零部件等技术进步，也使制成品本身趋于更轻、更小巧。

28.en: Businesses can locate based on other considerations, such as the availability of labour, while worrying less about the cost of delivering their output.
parts: 企业选址可以更多地考虑劳动力是否充足等其他因素，而不必像以往那样担心把产品运出去的成本。

30.en: But, behind the scenes, a series of technological innovations known broadly as containerisation and inter-modal transportation has led to swift productivity improvements in cargo-handling.
parts: 与此同时，一系列通常统称为集装箱化与多式联运的技术革新在幕后发挥了作用，货物装卸的效率迅速提高。

1.en: The vast expansion in international trade owes much to a revolution in the business of moving freight
parts: 国际贸易的大幅扩张，在很大程度上得益于货运业的一场变革。

3.en: While the global economy has been expanding at a bit over 3% a year, the volume of trade has been rising at a compound annual rate of about twice that.
parts: 全球经济的年增长率略高于3%，而贸易量的年均复合增长率约为这一水平的两倍。

7.en: The economic opening of countries that have traditionally been minor players is another.
parts: 另一个原因是，一些以往在国际贸易中只占次要地位的国家开放了经济。
terms: 处于次要地位的参与者

8.en: But one force behind the import-export boom has passed all but unnoticed: the rapidly falling cost of getting goods to market.
parts: 但促成进出口繁荣的一个因素几乎无人注意：把货物运到市场的成本正在迅速下降。

16.en: Countries still trade disproportionately with their geographic neighbours.
parts: 各国的对外贸易中，与地理位置相邻的国家之间的贸易仍占有格外高的比重。

19.en: As a result, less transportation is required for every dollar’s worth of imports or exports.
parts: 因此，同样价值一美元的进出口货物，现在需要的运输量更小。
terms: 每一美元所对应的价值

21.en: Most of the world’s disk-drive manufacturing is concentrated in South-east Asia.
parts: 全球的硬盘制造业大多集中在东南亚。

22.en: This is possible only because disk drives, while valuable, are small and light and so cost little to ship.
parts: 之所以能这样，是因为硬盘虽值钱，却体积小、重量轻，运费也就很低。

23.en: Computer manufacturers in Japan or Texas will not face hugely bigger freight bills if they import drives from Singapore rather than purchasing them on the domestic market.
parts: 日本或得克萨斯州的计算机厂商即便从新加坡进口硬盘，而不在国内市场采购，运费也不会高出多少。

24.en: Distance therefore poses no obstacle to the globalisation of the disk-drive industry.
parts: 因此，距离不会妨碍硬盘制造业的全球化。

31.en: Forty years ago, the process of exporting or importing involved a great many stages of handling, which risked portions of the shipment being damaged or stolen along the way.
parts: 四十年前，货物进出口要经过许多道装卸、搬运环节，部分货物可能在途中损坏或遭窃。

36.en: National governments, by and large, kept a much firmer hand on truck and railroad tariffs than on charges for ocean freight.
parts: 总的来说，各国政府对公路和铁路运价的管制，过去远比对海运收费的管制严格。
terms: kept a much firmer hand on
kept a much firmer hand on

38.en: First airlines, then road hauliers and railways, were freed from restrictions on what they could carry, where they could haul it and what price they could charge.
parts: 先是航空公司，随后是公路货运企业和铁路，都摆脱了种种限制，可以自己决定运什么、运到哪里、收多少运费。

44.en: Bringing these barriers down would help the world’s economies grow even closer.
parts: 消除这些障碍，有助于世界各经济体之间建立更紧密的联系。

2.en: International trade is growing at a startling pace.
parts: 国际贸易正以惊人的速度增长。

5.en: What lies behind this explosion in international commerce?
parts: 国际贸易为何会如此迅猛增长？

6.en: The general worldwide decline in trade barriers, such as customs duties and import quotas, is surely one explanation.
parts: 世界各地的贸易壁垒普遍减少，例如关税降低、进口配额限制放宽，这无疑是原因之一。

9.en: Theoretically, in the world of trade, shipping costs do not matter.
parts: 从理论上说，在贸易的世界里，运输成本无关紧要。

10.en: Goods, once they have been made, are assumed to move instantly and at no cost from place to place.
parts: 理论上假定，商品一经制成，就能立即从一地运到另一地，而且不产生任何费用。

11.en: The real world, however, is full of frictions.
parts: 然而在现实中，货物流通处处会遇到阻力。

15.en: But these sorts of products are heavy and bulky and the cost of transporting them relatively high.
parts: 但这类产品既重又占地方，运输成本也相对较高。

17.en: Over time, however, world output has shifted into goods whose worth is unrelated to their size and weight.
parts: 不过，随着时间推移，全球生产已转向那些价值与体积和重量无关的商品。

20.en: To see how this influences trade, consider the business of making disk drives for computers.
parts: 要看这种变化如何影响贸易，可以拿电脑磁盘驱动器的制造业为例。

25.en: This is even more true of the fast-growing information industries.
parts: 对于增长迅速的信息产业，距离更不成问题。

26.en: Films and compact discs cost little to transport, even by aeroplane.
parts: 影片和光盘即使用飞机运，费用也很低。

27.en: Computer software can be ‘exported’ without ever loading it onto a ship, simply by transmitting it over telephone lines from one country to another, so freight rates and cargo-handling schedules become insignificant factors in deciding where to make the product.
parts: 计算机软件根本不必装船，只需通过电话线从一国传送到另一国，就可以实现“出口”。
因此，决定在哪里生产软件时，货运费率和货物装卸时间安排都无足轻重。

29.en: In many countries deregulation has helped to drive the process along.
parts: 在许多国家，放松管制有助于推动这一进程。

33.en: By 1967, dual-purpose ships, carrying loose cargo in the hold and containers on the deck, were giving way to all-container vessels that moved thousands of boxes at a time.
parts: 到1967年，舱内装散货、甲板上装集装箱的两用船，正逐渐让位于一次能运数千个集装箱的全集装箱船。

34.en: The shipping container transformed ocean shipping into a highly efficient, intensely competitive business.
parts: 集装箱的出现使海运业变成了一个效率很高、竞争激烈的行业。

35.en: But getting the cargo to and from the dock was a different story.
parts: 但把货物运到码头或从码头运走，又是另一回事。

37.en: This started changing, however, in the mid-1970s, when America began to deregulate its transportation industry.
parts: 不过，到了20世纪70年代中期，美国开始放松对运输业的管制，情况也开始改变。

39.en: Big productivity gains resulted.
parts: 结果，生产率大幅提高。

40.en: Between 1985 and 1996, for example, America’s freight railways dramatically reduced their employment, trackage, and their fleets of locomotives - while increasing the amount of cargo they hauled.
parts: 例如，1985年至1996年间，美国的货运铁路公司大幅减少了员工人数、运营线路总长度和机车数量，
同期运送的货物却更多了。

41.en: Europe’s railways have also shown marked, albeit smaller, productivity improvements.
parts: 欧洲铁路的生产率也显著提高，只是增幅较小。

32.en: We hail as masterpieces the cave paintings in southern France and elsewhere, dating back some 20,000 years.
parts: 法国南部和其他地方的洞穴壁画距今约两万年，我们将它们奉为杰作。

9.en: However, in ants there is no cultural transmission – everything must be encoded in the genes – whereas in humans the opposite is true.
parts: 然而，蚂蚁没有文化传承，一切都必须编码在基因中，而人类的情况恰好相反。

26.en: Even more impressively, DNA analysis of the fungi suggests that the ants improve or modify the fungi by regularly swapping and sharing strains with neighbouring ant colonies.
parts: 更令人惊叹的是，对这些真菌的DNA分析表明，
蚂蚁会定期与邻近的蚁群交换、共享菌株，从而改良或改变这些真菌。

27.en: Whereas prehistoric man had no exposure to urban lifestyles - the forcing house of intelligence - the evidence suggests that ants have lived in urban settings for close on a hundred million years, developing and maintaining underground cities of specialised chambers and tunnels.
parts: 史前人类从未接触过城市生活，而这种生活方式有助于催生智慧。
相比之下，证据表明，蚂蚁已在城市环境中生活了近一亿年，
一直在建造和维护由专用巢室和通道组成的地下城市。

1.en: When we think of intelligent members of the animal kingdom, the creatures that spring immediately to mind are apes and monkeys.
parts: 一想到动物界的聪明成员，我们马上就会想到猿和猴。

5.en: Such chemical communication can be compared to the human use of visual and auditory channels (as in religious chants, advertising images and jingles, political slogans and martial music) to arouse and propagate moods and attitudes.
parts: 这种化学交流可以和人类利用视觉和听觉渠道的方式相比。
例如，人们借助宗教吟诵、广告图像和广告短曲、政治口号和军乐，
唤起并传播情绪和态度。

10.en: Only basic instincts are carried in the genes of a newborn baby, other skills being learned from others in the community as the child grows up.
parts: 新生儿通过基因承袭的只有基本本能；其他技能是在孩子长大的过程中向周围的人学来的。

13.en: Their fungus farming and aphid herding crafts are sophisticated when compared to the agricultural skills of humans five thousand years ago but have been totally overtaken by modern human agribusiness.
parts: 与五千年前人类的农业技术相比，蚂蚁种植真菌、放牧蚜虫的技艺相当先进，
但现代人类的农业产业已远远超过了它们。

17.en: Moreover, recent evidence suggests that the crop farming of ants may be more sophisticated and adaptable than was thought.
parts: 此外，近期证据表明，蚂蚁的耕作方式可能比过去认为的更精细，也更能适应变化。

24.en: Ulrich Mueller of Maryland and his colleagues genetically screened 862 different types of fungi taken from ants’ nests.
parts: 马里兰州的乌尔里希·穆勒和同事对取自蚁巢的862种不同真菌做了遗传筛查。

29.en: Yet Hoelldobler and Wilson’s magnificent work for ant lovers, The Ants, describes a supercolony of the ant Formica yessensis on the Ishikari Coast of Hokkaido.
parts: 然而，霍尔多布勒和威尔逊写给蚂蚁爱好者的杰作《蚂蚁》，
描述了一个生活在北海道石狩海岸、由Formica yessensis这种蚂蚁组成的超级蚁群。

31.en: Such enduring and intricately meshed levels of technical achievement outstrip by far anything achieved by our distant ancestors.
parts: 这些技术成就历久不衰，各个层面又紧密交织，远远超过了我们远古祖先所取得的任何成果。
要小心爱护这些小生命。”

6.en: The biologist Lewis Thomas wrote, ‘Ants are so much like human beings as to be an embarrassment.
parts: 生物学家刘易斯·托马斯写道：“蚂蚁与人类如此相像，简直让人觉得尴尬。

46.en: It’s no surprise that Edward Wilson, in his essay, ‘In the company of ants’, advises readers who ask what to do with the ants in their kitchen to: ‘Watch where you step.
parts: 难怪爱德华·威尔逊在《与蚂蚁为伴》一文中，
对那些问他该拿厨房里的蚂蚁怎么办的读者建议道：“留心脚下。

7.en: They farm fungi, raise aphids as livestock, launch armies to war, use chemical sprays to alarm and confuse enemies, capture slaves, engage in child labour, exchange information ceaselessly.
parts: 它们种植真菌，把蚜虫当作牲畜饲养，派出军队打仗，
喷出化学物质惊吓敌方、扰乱敌方，俘获奴隶，使用童工，还不停地交换信息。

7.en: And when did this event, or events, take place?
parts: 这次迁徙，或是这几次迁徙，发生在什么时候？

8.en: In recent years, new clues have come from research into genetics, including the distribution of genetic markers in modern Native Americans.
parts: 近年来，遗传学研究提供了新的线索，其中包括对当代美洲原住民遗传标记分布情况的研究。

9.en: An important project, led by the biological anthropologist Robert Williams, focused on the variants (called Gm allotypes) of one particular protein – immunoglobin G – found in the fluid portion of human blood.
parts: 生物人类学家罗伯特·威廉斯主持了一项重要研究，重点考察一种特定蛋白质的变体（称为 Gm 同种异型）。
这种蛋白质是免疫球蛋白G，存在于人体血液的液体成分中。

19.en: How far does other research support these conclusions?
parts: 其他研究在多大程度上支持这些结论？

20.en: Geneticist Douglas Wallace has studied mitochondrial DNA in blood samples from three widely separated Native American groups: Pima-Papago Indians in Arizona, Maya Indians on the Yucatán peninsula, Mexico, and Ticuna Indians in the Upper Amazon region of Brazil.
parts: 遗传学家道格拉斯·华莱士研究了三个相距很远的美洲原住民群体血样中的线粒体DNA。
这三个群体是亚利桑那州的皮马-帕帕戈人、墨西哥尤卡坦半岛的玛雅人和巴西亚马孙河上游地区的提库纳人。

25.en: Studies carried out by Turner of many thousands of New and Old World specimens, both ancient and modern, suggest that the majority of prehistoric Americans are linked to Northern Asian populations by crown and root traits such as incisor shoveling (a scooping out on one or both surfaces of the tooth), single-rooted upper first premolars and triple-rooted lower first molars.
parts: 特纳研究了新大陆和旧大陆数以千计的古代和现代标本。
研究表明，大多数史前美洲人与北亚人群之间的联系，可从一些牙冠和牙根特征看出来，
例如铲形门齿（牙齿的一面或两面呈凹陷状）、单根的上颌第一前磨牙和三根的下颌第一磨牙。

1.en: Study of the origins and distribution of human populations used to be based on archaeological and fossil evidence.
parts: 过去，对人群起源和分布的研究以考古证据和化石证据为依据。

2.en: A number of techniques developed since the 1950s, however, have placed the study of these subjects on a sounder and more objective footing.
parts: 不过，20世纪50年代以来发展起来的一些技术，使这些问题的研究有了更可靠、更客观的基础。

3.en: The best information on early population movements is now being obtained from the ‘archaeology of the living body’, the clues to be found in genetic material.
parts: 如今，要了解早期人群迁徙，最有价值的信息来自“活体考古”，也就是在遗传物质中找到的线索。

4.en: Recent work on the problem of when people first entered the Americas is an example of the value of these new techniques.
parts: 人类最初何时进入美洲？近期对这一问题的研究，便体现了这些新技术的价值。

5.en: North-east Asia and Siberia have long been accepted as the launching ground for the first human colonisers of the New World.
parts: 长期以来，人们一直认为，首批前往新大陆定居的人类是从东北亚和西伯利亚出发的。
terms: 长期以来一直被公认为

6.en: But was there one major wave of migration across the Bering Strait into the Americas, or several?
parts: 不过，当初跨越白令海峡进入美洲的大规模迁徙，究竟只有一波，还是有好几波？

10.en: All proteins ‘drift’, or produce variants, over the generations, and members of an interbreeding human population will share a set of such variants.
parts: 所有蛋白质在世代相传的过程中都会发生“漂变”，即产生变体。
同一人群的成员相互通婚，因而会共有一组这样的变体。

11.en: Thus, by comparing the Gm allotypes of two different populations (e.g. two Indian tribes), one can establish their genetic ‘distance’, which itself can be calibrated to give an indication of the length of time since these populations last interbred.
parts: 因此，比较两个不同人群（例如两个美洲原住民部族）的Gm同种异型，就能确定两者的遗传“距离”。
这种距离本身还可以加以校准，用来估计距这两个人群上一次通婚已过去多久。

12.en: Williams and his colleagues sampled the blood of over 5,000 American Indians in western North America during a twenty-year period.
parts: 在20年间，威廉斯和同事采集了北美西部5000多名美洲原住民的血样。

13.en: They found that their Gm allotypes could be divided into two groups, one of which also corresponded to the genetic typing of Central and South American Indians.
parts: 他们发现，这些人的Gm同种异型可分为两组，其中一组也与中美洲和南美洲原住民的遗传分型相符。
terms: 中美洲和南美洲原住民

14.en: Other tests showed that the Inuit (or Eskimo) and Aleut formed a third group.
parts: 其他检验表明，因纽特人（又称爱斯基摩人）和阿留申人构成了第三组。

15.en: From this evidence it was deduced that there had been three major waves of migration across the Bering Strait.
parts: 根据这些证据，研究者推断，人群曾分三大波跨越白令海峡迁徙。

16.en: The first, Paleo-Indian, wave more than 15,000 years ago was ancestral to all Central and South American Indians.
parts: 第一波迁徙发生在1.5万多年前。随这波迁徙而来的古印第安人，是所有中美洲和南美洲原住民的祖先。
terms: 中美洲和南美洲原住民

17.en: The second wave, about 14,000-12,000 years ago, brought Na-Dene hunters, ancestors of the Navajo and Apache (who only migrated south from Canada about 600 or 700 years ago).
parts: 第二波迁徙约在1.4万至1.2万年前，带来了纳-德内猎人，也就是纳瓦霍人和阿帕奇人的祖先。
（后面这两个族群直到约六七百年前才从加拿大向南迁徙。）

18.en: The third wave, perhaps 10,000 or 9,000 years ago, saw the migration from North-east Asia of groups ancestral to the modern Eskimo and Aleut.
parts: 第三波迁徙可能发生在1万年前或9000年前。当时，一些人群从东北亚迁出，他们是今天的爱斯基摩人和阿留申人的祖先。

21.en: As would have been predicted by Robert Williams’s work, all three groups appear to be descended from the same ancestral (Paleo-Indian) population.
parts: 正如从罗伯特·威廉斯的研究中可以预料的那样，这三个群体看来都源自同一个祖先人群，即古印第安人。

22.en: There are two other kinds of research that have thrown some light on the origins of the Native American population; they involve the study of teeth and of languages.
parts: 另有两类研究为美洲原住民的起源提供了一些线索，分别研究牙齿和语言。

23.en: The biological anthropologist Christy Turner is an expert in the analysis of changing physical characteristics in human teeth.
parts: 生物人类学家克里斯蒂·特纳专长于分析人类牙齿形态特征的变化。

24.en: He argues that tooth crowns and roots have a high genetic component, minimally affected by environmental and other factors.
parts: 他认为，牙冠和牙根在很大程度上取决于遗传，受环境及其他因素的影响很小。

26.en: According to Turner, this ties in with the idea of a single Paleo-Indian migration out of North Asia, which he sets at before 14,000 years ago by calibrating rates of dental micro-evolution.
parts: 特纳认为，这与古印第安人曾从北亚向外迁徙一次的说法相吻合。
他根据牙齿微进化速率进行校准，将这次迁徙定在距今1.4万年以前。

27.en: Tooth analyses also suggest that there were two later migrations of Na-Denes and Eskimo- Aleut.
parts: 牙齿分析还表明，后来又发生过两次迁徙，涉及纳-德内人和爱斯基摩-阿留申人。

28.en: The linguist Joseph Greenberg has, since the 1950s, argued that all Native American languages belong to a single ‘Amerind’ family, except for Na-Dene and Eskimo-Aleut - a view that gives credence to the idea of three main migrations.
parts: 自20世纪50年代以来，语言学家约瑟夫·格林伯格一直主张，除纳-德内语和爱斯基摩-阿留申语外，美洲原住民的所有语言都属于同一个“阿美林德”语系。
这一观点让三次主要迁徙的说法更可信。

29.en: Greenberg is in a minority among fellow linguists, most of whom favour the notion of a great many waves of migration to account for the more than 1,000 languages spoken at one time by American Indians.
parts: 格林伯格在语言学界属于少数派。
多数同行认为，美洲原住民一度使用过1000多种语言，要解释这一点，需要用许多次迁徙来说明。

30.en: But there is no doubt that the new genetic and dental evidence provides strong backing for Greenberg’s view.
parts: 不过，新的遗传学证据和牙齿研究证据，无疑为格林伯格的观点提供了有力支持。

31.en: Dates given for the migrations should nevertheless be treated with caution, except where supported by hard archaeological evidence.
parts: 尽管如此，对这些迁徙的年代仍应持谨慎态度，除非有确凿的考古证据予以支持。

2.en: Everyone accepts this as ‘biologically’ obvious.
parts: 大家都认为，从“生物学”的角度看，这一点显而易见。

4.en: However, in this statement we think of artificially produced, technical objects, products which are subjected to natural wear and tear during use.
parts: 然而，说这话时我们想到的是人工制造的技术产品，它们在使用过程中会自然磨损。

22.en: Every organism has a life span which is highly characteristic.
parts: 每种生物都有其特有的寿命。

28.en: Like the life span, the metabolic rate has for different organisms a fixed mathematical relationship to the body mass.
parts: 与寿命一样，不同生物的代谢率与其体重之间也存在固定的数学关系。

29.en: In comparison to the life span this relationship is ‘inverted’: the larger the organism the lower its metabolic rate.
parts: 与寿命和体重的关系相比，代谢率与体重的关系恰好“相反”：生物体越大，代谢率就越低。

1.en: Our life span is restricted.
parts: 我们的寿命是有限的。

3.en: ‘Nothing lives for ever!’
parts: “没有什么能永远活下去！”

5.en: This leads to the result that at some time or other the object stops working and is unusable (‘death’ in the biological sense).
parts: 结果是，这种物品迟早会停止运转，再也无法使用（相当于生物学意义上的“死亡”）。

6.en: But are the wear and tear and loss of function of technical objects and the death of living organisms really similar or comparable?
parts: 可是，人造设备的磨损和功能丧失，与生物体的死亡，真的相似或具有可比性吗？

7.en: Our ’dead’ products are ‘static’, closed systems.
parts: 我们制造的这些“没有生命”的产品，是“静态”的封闭系统。

8.en: It is always the basic material which constitutes the object and which, in the natural course of things, is worn down and becomes ‘older’.
parts: 构成物品的始终是原来那些基本材料；随着时间推移，磨损、变“老”的也是这些材料。
terms: in the natural course of things
in the natural course of things

9.en: Ageing in this case must occur according to the laws of physical chemistry and of thermodynamics.
parts: 在这种情况下，老化必然遵循物理化学和热力学规律。

10.en: Although the same law holds for a living organism, the result of this law is not inexorable in the same way.
parts: 同样的规律虽然也适用于生物体，但它在生物体上造成的后果，却未必像在人造物品上那样不可避免。

11.en: At least as long as a biological system has the ability to renew itself it could actually become older without ageing; an organism is an open, dynamic system through which new material continuously flows.
parts: 至少，只要生物系统还能自我更新，它的年龄就有可能增长而不发生衰老；
生物体是开放的动态系统，不断有新的物质流经其中。

12.en: Destruction of old material and formation of new material are thus in permanent dynamic equilibrium.
parts: 因此，旧物质不断分解，新物质不断形成，两者始终保持动态平衡。

13.en: The material of which the organism is formed changes continuously.
parts: 构成生物体的物质在不断变化。

14.en: Thus our bodies continuously exchange old substance for new, just like a spring which more or less maintains its form and movement, but in which the water molecules are always different.
parts: 因此，我们的身体不断以新物质替代旧物质，就像一眼泉水：它的形态和流动方式大体不变，里面的水分子却一直在更换。

15.en: Thus ageing and death should not be seen as inevitable, particularly as the organism possesses many mechanisms for repair.
parts: 因此，不应把衰老和死亡看作必然，尤其是考虑到生物体本身具有许多修复机制。

16.en: It is not, in principle, necessary for a biological system to age and die.
parts: 从原理上说，生物系统并非一定要衰老和死亡。

17.en: Nevertheless, a restricted life span, ageing, and then death are basic characteristics of life.
parts: 然而，寿命有限、逐渐衰老并最终死亡，都是生命的基本特征。

18.en: The reason for this is easy to recognise: in nature, the existent organisms either adapt or are regularly replaced by new types.
parts: 其中的原因并不难理解：在自然界中，现有的生物要么适应环境，要么不断被新的类型取代。

19.en: Because of changes in the genetic material (mutations) these have new characteristics and in the course of their individual lives they are tested for optimal or better adaptation to the environmental conditions.
parts: 由于遗传物质发生变化（突变），这些新类型具有了新的特征。
在每个个体的一生中，这些特征会受到检验，看它们是否最适应环境，或至少适应得更好。

20.en: Immortality would disturb this system - it needs room for new and better life.
parts: 永生会打乱这一系统，因为它需要为新的、更能适应环境的生命留出空间。

21.en: This is the basic problem of evolution.
parts: 这就是进化所面对的基本问题。

23.en: There are striking differences in life span between different species, but within one species the parameter is relatively constant.
parts: 不同物种的寿命有显著差异，但在同一物种内部，这个数值相对恒定。

24.en: For example, the average duration of human life has hardly changed in thousands of years.
parts: 例如，几千年来，人类寿命的平均长度几乎没有改变。

25.en: Although more and more people attain an advanced age as a result of developments in medical care and better nutrition, the characteristic upper limit for most remains 80 years.
parts: 医疗条件和营养水平的改善使越来越多的人活到高龄，但对大多数人来说，通常的寿命上限仍是80岁。

26.en: A further argument against the simple wear and tear theory is the observation that the time within which organisms age lies between a few days (even a few hours for unicellular organisms) and several thousand years, as with mammoth trees.
parts: 还有一种观察结果也不支持单纯的磨损理论：
不同生物发生衰老的时程短则几天（单细胞生物甚至只需几小时），长则数千年，巨杉便是例子。

27.en: If a life span is a genetically determined biological characteristic, it is logically necessary to propose the existence of an internal clock, which in some way measures and controls the ageing process and which finally determines death as the last step in a fixed programme.
parts: 如果寿命是由遗传决定的生物特性，那么从逻辑上就有必要提出一个假设，即生物体内存在一座时钟。
这座时钟以某种方式计量并控制衰老过程，最终决定固定程序的最后一步——死亡。

30.en: Again this relationship is valid not only for birds, but also, similarly on average within the systematic unit, for all other organisms (plants, animals, unicellular organisms).
parts: 这种关系同样不只适用于鸟类；对其他所有生物（植物、动物和单细胞生物）来说，在各自分类单元内按平均值来看，也有同样的关系。

31.en: Animals which behave ‘frugally’ with energy become particularly old, for example, crocodiles and tortoises.
parts: 在能量使用上很“节俭”的动物格外长寿，比如鳄鱼和陆龟。

32.en: Parrots and birds of prey are often held chained up.
parts: 人们常用链子拴养鹦鹉和猛禽。

33.en: Thus they are not able to ‘experience life’ and so they attain a high life span in captivity.
parts: 因此，它们无法“体验生活”，也正因如此，它们在圈养环境下能活得很久。

34.en: Animals which save energy by hibernation or lethargy (e. g. bats or hedgehogs) live much longer than those which are always active.
parts: 通过冬眠或蛰伏节省能量的动物（如蝙蝠和刺猬），比一直活跃的动物长寿得多。

35.en: The metabolic rate of mice can be reduced by a very low consumption of food (hunger diet).
parts: 小鼠摄入极少量食物（饥饿饮食）时，代谢率会降低。

36.en: They then may live twice as long as their well fed comrades.
parts: 这样一来，它们的寿命可能达到那些食物充足的同伴的两倍。

37.en: Women become distinctly (about 10 per cent) older than men.
parts: 女性比男性明显长寿，寿命约长10%。

38.en: If you examine the metabolic rates of the two sexes you establish that the higher male metabolic rate roughly accounts for the lower male life span.
parts: 考察两性的代谢率可以发现，男性的代谢率较高，这大致可以解释男性寿命较短的现象。

39.en: That means that they live life ‘energetically’ - more intensively, but not for as long.
parts: 也就是说，男性以一种“耗能较多”的方式生活——强度更高，时间却没那么长。
terms: 精力旺盛地（呼应能量消耗）

40.en: It follows from the above that sparing use of energy reserves should tend to extend life.
parts: 由以上论述可以推知，节省使用储备能量应当有助于延长寿命。
terms: 应当倾向于；可能有助于

41.en: Extreme high performance sports may lead to optimal cardiovascular performance, but they quite certainly do not prolong life.
parts: 极高强度的竞技运动或许可以使心血管功能达到最佳状态，但它们确实不能延长寿命。

42.en: Relaxation lowers metabolic rate, as does adequate sleep and in general an equable and balanced personality.
parts: 放松能降低代谢率；充足的睡眠也有这种作用。一般来说，平和、稳重的性格同样如此。

43.en: Each of us can develop his or her own ‘energy saving programme’ with a little self-observation, critical self-control and, above all, logical consistency.
parts: 只要稍加自我观察，审慎地进行自我调节，尤其是做到前后一致，我们每个人都能制定自己的“节能计划”。

44.en: Experience will show that to live in this way not only increases the life span but is also very healthy.
parts: 经验将会表明，这样生活不仅能延长寿命，而且很有益于健康。

45.en: This final aspect should not be forgotten.
parts: 最后这一点也应当记住。

32.en: In the Yukon and Kuskokwim rivers, chinook and chum runs were probably the poorest since statehood; subsistence communities throughout the region, who normally have priority over commercial fishing, were devastated.
parts: 在育空河和库斯科奎姆河，帝王鲑和狗鲑的洄游数量很可能是阿拉斯加建州以来最少的。
整个地区依靠捕鱼维生的社区都遭受了沉重打击，而这些社区捕鱼通常享有优先于商业捕捞的权利。
terms: 依靠当地资源维生的社区

1.en: More than two hundred years ago, Russian explorers and fur hunters landed on the Aleutian Islands, a volcanic archipelago in the North Pacific, and learned of a land mass that lay farther to the north.
parts: 两百多年前，俄国探险家和毛皮猎人登上了阿留申群岛，那是北太平洋的一组火山岛。
他们还得知更北边有一片陆地。

5.en: The rivers feed into the Bering Sea and Gulf of Alaska - cold, nutrient-rich waters which support tens of millions of seabirds, and over 400 species of fish, shellfish, crustaceans, and molluscs.
parts: 这些河流注入白令海和阿拉斯加湾。那里寒冷而富含养分的水域，
养育着数千万只海鸟，以及四百多种鱼类、贝类、甲壳类和软体动物。

7.en: According to the Alaska Department of Fish and Game (ADF&G), Alaska’s commercial fisheries landed hundreds of thousands of tonnes of shellfish and herring, and well over a million tonnes of groundfish (cod, sole, perch and pollock) in 2000.
parts: 据阿拉斯加州渔猎局（ADF&G）统计，2000年阿拉斯加商业渔业捕获上岸的贝类和鲱鱼达数十万吨，
底层鱼类（鳕鱼、鳎鱼、鲈鱼和狭鳕）的捕获量则远超一百万吨。

9.en: ‘Salmon,’ notes writer Susan Ewing in The Great Alaska Nature Factbook, ‘pump through Alaska like blood through a heart, bringing rhythmic, circulating nourishment to land, animals and people.’
parts: 作家苏珊·尤因在《阿拉斯加自然知识大全》中写道：“鲑鱼游遍阿拉斯加，犹如血液流经心脏，
给这片土地、这里的动物和人带来循环往复、富有节律的滋养。”

10.en: The ‘predictable abundance of salmon allowed some native cultures to flourish,’ and ‘dying spawners feed bears, eagles, other animals, and ultimately the soil itself.’
parts: 鲑鱼“总会如期大量出现，使一些原住民文化得以繁荣”，而“产卵后濒死的鲑鱼滋养着熊、鹰和其他动物，最终还滋养了土壤本身”。

11.en: All five species of Pacific salmon - chinook, or king; chum, or dog; coho, or silver; sockeye, or red; and pink, or humpback - spawn in Alaskan waters, and 90% of all Pacific salmon commercially caught in North America are produced there.
parts: 五种太平洋鲑鱼，包括帝王鲑（又称王鲑）、大麻哈鱼（又称狗鲑）、银鲑、红鲑和粉红鲑（又称驼背鲑），都在阿拉斯加水域产卵。
北美商业捕捞的太平洋鲑鱼中，有90%产自那里。

31.en: Some observers thought the Alaska salmon fisheries would not have any chance of certification when, in the months leading up to MSC’s final decision, salmon runs throughout western Alaska completely collapsed.
parts: 一些观察人士当时认为，阿拉斯加鲑鱼渔业根本没有获得认证的机会：
在海洋管理委员会作出最终决定前的几个月里，整个阿拉斯加西部的鲑鱼洄游数量骤减。
terms: would not have any chance of
would not have any chance of
in the months leading up to
in the months leading up to

2.en: The islands’ native inhabitants called this land mass Aleyska, the ‘Great Land’; today, we know it as Alaska.
parts: 岛上的原住民称这片陆地为Aleyska，意为“伟大的土地”；今天我们称它为阿拉斯加。

15.en: Between 1940 and 1959, overfishing led to crashes in salmon populations so severe that in 1953 Alaska was declared a federal disaster area.
parts: 1940年至1959年间，过度捕捞导致鲑鱼种群数量锐减，情况极其严重，以至于1953年阿拉斯加被宣布为联邦灾区。

16.en: With the onset of statehood, however, the State of Alaska took over management of its own fisheries, guided by a state constitution which mandates that Alaska’s natural resources be managed on a sustainable basis.
parts: 不过，阿拉斯加成为美国的一个州后，接管了本州的渔业管理。
州政府依照州宪法办事，宪法规定阿拉斯加的自然资源必须以可持续的方式管理。

23.en: The fishermen know the approximate time of year when they will be allowed to fish, but on any given day, one or more field biologists in a particular area can put a halt to fishing.
parts: 渔民知道每年大致什么时候可以捕鱼，
但在任何一天，某个地区的一名或多名野外生物学家都可以叫停当地的捕捞活动。

34.en: Rather, they contend, it was almost certainly the result of climatic shifts, prompted in part by cumulative effects of the el niño / la niña phenomenon on Pacific Ocean temperatures, culminating in a harsh winter in which huge numbers of salmon eggs were frozen.
parts: 他们认为，这几乎可以肯定是气候变化所致。
厄尔尼诺和拉尼娜现象对太平洋水温的累积影响，是引发这种气候变化的部分原因；
最终出现了一个严冬，大量鲑鱼卵被冻住。

18.en: Over the next few decades average catches steadily increased as a result of this policy of sustainable management, until, during the 1990s, annual harvests were well in excess of 100 million, and on several occasions over 200 million fish.
parts: 在随后的几十年里，这一可持续管理政策使平均捕捞量稳步上升。
到20世纪90年代，每年的捕捞量已远超一亿条，有好几年还超过了两亿条。

25.en: It is this management mechanism that has allowed Alaska salmon stocks - and, accordingly, Alaska salmon fisheries - to prosper, even as salmon populations in the rest of the United States are increasingly considered threatened or even endangered.
parts: 正是这种管理机制使阿拉斯加的鲑鱼资源得以兴旺，也因此使当地鲑鱼渔业得以繁荣。
与此同时，在美国其他地区，鲑鱼种群却日益被视为受到威胁，甚至濒临灭绝。

30.en: The MSC then appoints a certification committee, composed of a panel of fisheries experts, which gathers information and opinions from fishermen, biologists, government officials, industry representatives, non-governmental organisations and others.
parts: 随后，海洋管理委员会任命一个由渔业专家组成的认证委员会。
该委员会向渔民、生物学家、政府官员、行业代表、非政府组织及其他各方收集信息和意见。

9.en: But on any given day, what Schaefer can offer is typical for today’s drugs rep - a car trunk full of promotional gifts and gadgets, a budget that could buy lunches and dinners for a small country, hundreds of free drug samples and the freedom to give a physician $200 to prescribe her new product to the next six patients who fit the drug’s profile.
parts: 不过，舍费尔平日能拿出的东西，在如今的医药代表中很常见：一后备厢的促销礼品和小玩意儿，
一笔足够请一个小国的人吃午饭和晚饭的预算，数百份免费药品样品，
她还有权给医生200美元，请对方给接下来六位符合用药条件的患者开她推销的新药。
terms: 在任何一个寻常的日子里
符合这种药的用药条件

10.en: And she also has a few $1,000 honoraria to offer in exchange for doctors’ attendance at her company’s next educational lecture.
parts: 此外，她还能提供几份酬金，每份1,000美元，请医生出席她公司下一场教育讲座。

3.en: A few months ago Kim Schaefer, sales representative of a major global pharmaceutical company, walked into a medical center in New York to bring information and free samples of her company’s latest products.
parts: 几个月前，一家大型跨国制药公司的销售代表金·舍费尔走进纽约的一家医疗中心，
向那里的人介绍公司的最新产品，并送去免费样品。

12.en: Salespeople like Schaefer walk the line between the common practice of buying a prospect’s time with a free meal, and bribing doctors to prescribe their drugs.
parts: 像舍费尔这样的销售人员，游走在两种做法的界线之间：一种是常见的做法，请潜在客户吃一顿饭，以换取对方的时间，
另一种则是贿赂医生，让他们开自己推销的药。
terms: 游走在两者的界线之间

15.en: The explosion in the sheer number of salespeople in the field – and the amount of funding used to promote their causes – forces close examination of the pressures, influences and relationships between drug reps and doctors.
parts: 这一行的销售人员数量猛增，投入推广活动的资金也大幅增加，
这迫使人们仔细审视医药代表与医生之间的压力、影响和关系。

20.en: The flashy brochures and pamphlets left by the sales reps are often followed up with meals at expensive restaurants, meetings in warm and sunny places, and an inundation of promotional gadgets.
parts: 医药代表留下花哨的产品手册和宣传册后，往往还会请医生到高档餐厅用餐、
安排他们在温暖晴朗的地方开会，再送上大量促销小礼品。

30.en: A total of 131 doctors self-reported their prescribing patterns - the conclusion was that the availability of samples led them to dispense and prescribe drugs that differed from their preferred drug choice.
parts: 共有131名医生自行报告了各自的处方习惯。
研究得出的结论是，有样品可用，使医生配发和开具的药物与他们原本首选的药物不同。

1.en: Pharmaceuticals is one of the most profitable industries in North America.
parts: 制药业是北美最赚钱的行业之一。

4.en: That day she was lucky - a doctor was available to see her.
parts: 那天她很幸运，有一位医生有空见她。

11.en: Selling pharmaceuticals is a daily exercise in ethical judgement.
parts: 销售药品需要每天作出道德判断。

16.en: Salespeople provide much-needed information and education to physicians.
parts: 销售人员向医生提供他们急需的信息和培训。

17.en: In many cases the glossy brochures, article reprints and prescriptions they deliver are primary sources of drug education for healthcare givers.
parts: 在许多情况下，医药代表送来的光面宣传册、文章抽印本和处方，是医护人员了解药品知识的主要来源。

18.en: With the huge investment the industry has placed in face-to-face selling, salespeople have essentially become specialists in one drug or group of drugs – a tremendous advantage in getting the attention of busy doctors in need of quick information.
parts: 这个行业在面对面销售上投入巨大，销售人员实际上已成了某种或某一类药品的专家。
忙碌的医生需要快速获取信息，这让医药代表在吸引他们的注意力时占有很大优势。

22.en: Millions of dollars are spent by pharmaceutical companies on promotional products like coffee mugs, shirts, umbrellas, and golf balls.
parts: 制药公司在促销品上花费数百万美元，例如咖啡杯、衬衫、雨伞和高尔夫球。

31.en: The bottom line is that pharmaceutical companies as a whole invest more in marketing than they do in research and development.
parts: 归根结底，制药公司总体上在营销方面的投资比研发投入更多。

34.en: But as the medical world continues to grapple with what’s acceptable and what’s not, it is clear that companies must continue to be heavily scrutinized for their sales and marketing strategies.
parts: 不过，医学界仍在努力厘清哪些做法可以接受、哪些不能接受。
有一点很清楚：制药公司的销售与营销策略必须继续受到严格审视。

19.en: But the sales push rarely stops in the office.
parts: 但推销活动很少止于医生的诊室。

13.en: They work in an industry highly criticized for its sales and marketing practices, but find themselves in the middle of the age-old chicken-or-egg question – businesses won’t use strategies that don’t work, so are doctors to blame for the escalating extravagance of pharmaceutical marketing?
parts: 他们所在的行业因销售和营销手法备受批评，却又陷入了那个由来已久的“先有鸡还是先有蛋”的问题：
企业不会采用无效的策略，那么，医药营销越来越铺张，医生该不该为此负责？

21.en: Rarely do patients watch a doctor write with a pen that isn’t emblazoned with a drug’s name, or see a nurse use a tablet not bearing a pharmaceutical company’s logo.
parts: 病人很少看到医生用一支没有醒目药名的笔写字，
也很少看到护士用一本没有制药公司标志的便笺簿。

30.en: In less enlightened countries, and in the European Union, the trend has been to reduce rather than eliminate subsidies and to introduce new payments to encourage farmers to treat their land in environmentally friendlier ways, or to leave it fallow.
parts: 在一些观念较为保守的国家以及欧盟，政策趋向于削减补贴，而非彻底取消，
并增设补助，鼓励农民以更环保的方式利用土地，或让土地休耕。

11.en: Higher yields have been achieved by increased irrigation, better crop breeding, and a doubling in the use of pesticides and chemical fertilisers in the 1970s and 1980s.
parts: 20世纪70和80年代，灌溉增加、作物育种改进，加上农药和化肥用量翻了一番，使作物获得了更高的产量。

22.en: Fertiliser use doubled in Denmark in the period 1960-1985 and increased in The Netherlands by 150 per cent.
parts: 1960至1985年间，丹麦的化肥用量翻了一番，荷兰的用量则增加了150%。
terms: 增幅为百分之一百五十

4.en: There had, of course, been dictionaries in the past, the first of these being a little book of some 120 pages, compiled by a certain Robert Cawdray, published in 1604 under the title A Table Alphabeticall ‘of hard usuall English wordes’.
parts: 当然，早先就有词典。其中最早的一部是一本约120页的小书，
由一位名叫罗伯特·考德里的人编成，于1604年出版，题名《字母顺序表》，收录的是“常用英语难词”。

2.en: Specifically, Milgram told each volunteer ‘teacher-subject’ that the experiment was in the noble cause of education, and was designed to test whether or not punishing pupils for their mistakes would have a positive effect on the pupils’ ability to learn.
parts: 具体来说，米尔格拉姆告诉每个以“教师”身份参加实验的志愿者，这项实验是为了教育这一崇高事业，
目的是检验因学生犯错而惩罚他们，是否会对他们的学习能力产生积极影响。
terms: 扮演教师的实验参与者

2.en: This is not just because of the importance of English-speaking countries such as the USA in scientific research; the scientists of many non-English-speaking countries find that they need to write their research papers in English to reach a wide international audience.
parts: 这不仅是因为美国等英语国家在科学研究中占有重要地位。
许多非英语国家的科学家发现，要让世界各地更多人读到自己的研究，他们就得用英语撰写论文。
terms: English-speaking countries such as the USA
English-speaking countries such as the USA

19.en: But caloric-restriction projects underway in two species more closely related to humans - rhesus and squirrel monkeys - have made scientists optimistic that CR mimetics could help people.
parts: 不过，目前正对两种与人类亲缘关系较近的猴开展热量限制研究，分别是恒河猴和松鼠猴。
这些研究使科学家乐观地认为，模拟热量限制作用的物质可能对人有益。
terms: 模拟热量限制作用的物质

28.en: The best-studied candidate for a caloric-restriction mimetic, 2DG (2-deoxy-D-glucose), works by interfering with the way cells process glucose.
parts: 在有望模拟热量限制效果的物质中，研究最充分的是2DG（2-脱氧-D-葡萄糖）。
它通过干扰细胞处理葡萄糖的方式起作用。

1.en: In government laboratories and elsewhere, scientists are seeking a drug able to prolong life and youthful vigor.
parts: 在政府实验室和其他地方，科学家们正在寻找一种既能延长寿命、又能让青春活力保持得更久的药物。

7.en: Few mortals could stick to that harsh a regimen, especially for years on end.
parts: 很少有人能坚持如此严苛的饮食方案，尤其是要一连坚持好几年。

8.en: But what if someone could create a pill that mimicked the physiological effects of eating less without actually forcing people to eat less?
parts: 但是，假如有人能制成一种药丸，既能模拟少吃带来的生理效应，又无须真的迫使人们少吃，那会怎样呢？

11.en: No compound that would safely achieve the same feat in people has been found yet, but the search has been informative and has fanned hope that caloric-restriction (CR) mimetics can indeed be developed eventually.
parts: 迄今还没有找到能在人身上安全取得相同效果的化合物，
但探索过程带来了有益的发现，也让人们更加期待：最终确实有望研制出模拟热量限制（CR）效果的物质。

12.en: The benefits of caloric restriction
parts: 热量限制的益处

18.en: Until fairly recently, the studies were limited to short-lived creatures genetically distant from humans.
parts: 直到不久前，这些研究的对象还仅限于寿命短、在遗传上与人类亲缘关系较远的生物。

20.en: The monkey projects demonstrate that, compared with control animals that eat normally, caloric-restricted monkeys have lower body temperatures and levels of the pancreatic hormone insulin, and they retain more youthful levels of certain hormones that tend to fall with age.
parts: 猴子实验表明，与正常进食的对照动物相比，
摄入热量受限的猴子体温较低，胰腺分泌的胰岛素水平也较低。
某些激素通常会随年龄增长而下降，而这些猴子的此类激素仍保持在更接近年轻时的水平。

29.en: It has proved toxic at some doses in animals and so cannot be used in humans.
parts: 动物研究已证实，它在某些剂量下有毒，因此不能用于人体。

30.en: But it has demonstrated that chemicals can replicate the effects of caloric restriction; the trick is finding the right one.
parts: 不过，它表明化学物质可以模拟限制热量摄入的效果；关键是找对那种物质。

31.en: Cells use the glucose from food to generate ATP (adenosine triphosphate), the molecule that powers many activities in the body.
